forks.title: What the end-of-design scaffold commit contains when a design adds events or commands

card.problem: What does the end-of-design scaffold commit contain when a design adds events or commands? The scaffolder writes whole new files only. A new read model or policy that names a proposed event refers to a symbol that exists only as a fragment, so the commit does not typecheck (probe G: TS2339). ESAS-304's ticket says /build places fragments. ESAS-289 and ESAS-292 found that this leaves the owner's 'one commit with everything agreed' thin, or red.
useCases: A design adds event 'Ui Widget Layout Archived' on an existing aggregate plus a read model projecting it (teselly analytics)
A design adds only a read model over existing events
A design adds a brand-new kixie aggregate (needs one barrel line in @kixie/schemas)

options.label: Mechanical only: create-only scaffolder + guarded EOF barrel append; any file that names a fragment-only symbol is deferred to STILL OWED for /build

walks.text: Read model deferred; commit is thin but green
walks.given: a design adding event UiWidgetLayoutArchived and a read model projecting it
walks.then: the commit holds no read model, the report lists it as deferred, and the typecheck passes

walks.text: Identical across options
walks.given: a design adding only a read model over existing events
walks.then: the read model is written unregistered and the typecheck passes

options.label: Mechanical + placement: as A, then an agent in /design places topology fragments (new commands, events, their schemas; never registration), re-runs the scaffolder, and commits only if the repo's typecheck passes

walks.text: Everything agreed lands in one green commit
walks.given: a design adding event UiWidgetLayoutArchived and a read model projecting it
walks.then: the event fragment and its schema are placed, the read model is written unregistered, the typecheck passes, and one commit holds both

walks.text: Caught before commit
walks.given: the placing agent puts the event in the wrong namespace
walks.then: the step stops red with no commit and reports the failing file

options.label: Leave it red: commit everything; the scaffold commit may fail typecheck and /build fixes it

walks.text: Red commit
walks.given: a design adding event UiWidgetLayoutArchived and a read model projecting it
walks.then: the commit fails typecheck with TS2339 until /build places the event

options.rejectedBecause: Breaks the owner's stated bar 'the scaffold commit must build'.

recommendation.why: Only B delivers 'one commit with all the scaffolding agreed' when a design adds events, which most designs do. The typecheck gate makes the agent's edit safe. A is the floor B builds on (the scaffolder stays create-only plus the barrel append, ESAS-292 and ESAS-300), so B costs one extra agent step in ESAS-304.

card.ifOverturned: A: ESAS-304 keeps 'fragments never written in /design', and the report is honest that the commit is partial. C is ruled out by the owner's bar.

forks.title: ESAS-304 · What counts as 'agreed' on the eventstorming board for the design-end scaffold

card.problem: design.json has no accept state (DesignFile = propose/modify/remove/comments, BP design.ts:142-154; DesignStatus proposed|modified|removed|satisfied, nodes.ts:14). The scaffolder plans every coherent design.propose entry not yet extracted (filterDesign plan.ts:74). 'Everything agreed on both boards' therefore has no ES-side meaning today.
useCases: An AI proposal nobody discussed
A proposal with an unresolved comment questioning it
A human proposal
A proposal withdrawn by remove

options.label: Everything proposed and coherent is agreed (today's planner semantics)

walks.text: Diverges: scaffolds what is still being questioned.
walks.given: an AI-proposed policy carries an unresolved comment 'wrong module?'
walks.when: /design ends and the scaffold commit runs
walks.then: the policy is scaffolded into one module; the open question is answered by a committed file nobody agreed to

options.label: Explicit accept step on the ES layer (new design-layer state + op in BP, unowned in this run)

walks.text: Needs a blueprint-schema bump, both stores and board UI; no ticket owns it.
walks.given: the same policy, never accepted
walks.then: it is held and the report lists it 'held: not accepted'; every element needs a human Accept click first

options.label: Proposed and coherent, minus any element with an unresolved comment anchored on it

walks.text: Uses state the layer already has (DesignComment.resolved, commentAnchorKey).
walks.given: the same policy with an unresolved comment
walks.then: it is held with 'held: open comment <id>' and every other proposal scaffolds

recommendation.why: Expresses 'not agreed yet' with state the layer already has and no new BP work; held elements are visible in the report; B is the long-term answer to file if an explicit Accept gesture is wanted.

card.ifOverturned: A: the report has no 'held' section and open questions get scaffolded. B: file a blueprint ticket for an accept op and hold the scaffold step on it.

forks.title: ESAS-304 · S-transport: how agreed scenarios reach the scaffold run

status.reason: merged into ESAS-306-F3: one carrier for scenarios AND observations: the committed MapFile export, read by --map

card.problem: Only design.json and graph.json reach a scaffolder (VERIFIED-FACTS 0.6); the lane snapshot has no ops.jsonl, and hosted scenarios live in the server's design_maps. The plugin's committed map.json and anything committed do reach lanes (provisioner.md:88-95). Depends on ESAS-287's S-store choice.
useCases: Local session (ops.jsonl)
Hosted session (server design_maps)
Fleet lane with no .blueprint/
Re-run after a scenario was struck

options.label: Plugin exports agreed scenarios to a committed scenarios.json and passes --scenarios <file> to the declared scaffold command

walks.text: Works in all four use cases; framework-agnostic plain Gherkin shape owned by ESAS-287.
walks.given: SCN-a is agreed and SCN-b proposed in a hosted session
walks.then: scenarios.json holds SCN-a only, is committed with the report, the scaffolder reads it via --scenarios, and a lane later reads the same file from git

options.label: Each scaffolder reads the scenario store itself

walks.text: Diverges: silent zero in lanes; couples both scaffolders to both folds.
walks.given: a fleet lane with only the design snapshot
walks.then: it finds no ops.jsonl and no server credential and plans no scenario tests

walks.text: Diverges: conflates the ES layer with map entries and needs a design-schema bump.
walks.given: a hosted session whose scenarios live in the server
walks.then: design.json has no writer for them and carries nothing

recommendation.why: The only option that works for local, hosted and lane alike; the committed file is also the provenance of test names. ESAS-304 produces it, ESAS-287 owns the type, ESAS-302/303 read --scenarios.

card.ifOverturned: B: ESAS-302/303 each take a store dependency and lanes need the snapshot widened. C: ESAS-287 adds a design.json section and a hosted writer.

forks.title: ESAS-304 · Where the scaffold commit happens in a fleet

card.problem: In a fleet the owner is present only at the /design-multi sitting; a lane's /design is unattended with no .blueprint/ (unit-lane.md:81), and design.json carries no ticket attribution, so one unit's share of a shared design cannot be selected. /start-multi already gates orchestrator-authored base commits on int/<run-id> (start-multi.md:83).
useCases: A design-time scaffolder block in a fleet
Two units whose designs touch the same module
A unit with no ES design

options.label: Each lane's /design scaffolds from its snapshot

walks.text: Diverges: duplicate stubs and unanswerable blocks.
walks.given: two units share one design.json
walks.then: each scaffolds the whole delta, so both branches carry the other's stubs, and a block fires with no owner present and becomes a post-sitting escalation

options.label: One fleet scaffold commit: orchestrator dry-runs before the sitting, /start-multi step 0 commits on int/<run-id>, gated in baseGate

walks.text: Adds a pre-sitting dry-run to design-multi.md and a step-0 commit to start-multi.md.
walks.given: the same two units
walks.then: one commit with one report sits on int/<run-id>, each lane's /plan assigns stubs by designs:, and blocks were already answered at the sitting

options.label: v1 is single-unit /design only; fleets keep per-slice scaffolding

walks.text: Diverges from the owner's ask for fleets.
walks.given: a fleet run
walks.then: nothing changes from today: no design-end commit, blocks still fire inside build lanes

recommendation.why: The only option where blocks surface while the owner is present and 'one commit of everything agreed' survives a fleet.

card.ifOverturned: A: the lane /design escalates every block and the merge carries duplicate stubs. C: file the fleet path as a follow-up.

forks.title: ESAS-304 · An agreed scenario with no test at landing: block or warn

card.problem: ORIGIN 12c, never answered. The verifier rule (D8) refuses a pending scenario test in a delivered slice; this fork is about an agreed scenario with no test at all (scaffolder had no home, test deleted). Also framed from ESAS-287; the sitting keeps one.
useCases: A What scenario whose unit test was scaffolded and filled
A How scenario spanning two tickets in a fleet
A scenario the scaffolder could not place (still-owed)

options.label: Block every PR: every agreed scenario must map to a non-pending test in the branch

walks.text: Diverges: blocks the wrong unit.
walks.given: a How scenario owned by sibling unit Y
walks.then: X is blocked on a scenario only Y delivers

options.label: Warn: PR body and /merge-multi list agreed scenarios with no test

walks.text: An agreed example can ship untested.
walks.given: SCN-x the scaffolder could not place
walks.then: the body says 'SCN-x: no test (still-owed: no home)' and the merge proceeds

options.label: Warn on unit PRs; block at the integrated tree (/merge-multi, or a lone unit's /verify-build)

walks.text: Blocks only where every scenario's owner is present.
walks.given: a How scenario spanning units X and Y
walks.when: X's PR opens, then /merge-multi integrates X and Y
walks.then: X only warns, and at integration the scenario has its test so nothing blocks

walks.text: The commitment is enforced once.
walks.given: SCN-x with no test anywhere
walks.then: it blocks until the owner strikes SCN-x or a test is written

recommendation.why: An agreed example is a commitment and should block somewhere; the integrated tree is the first place every scenario's owner is present, and blocking a unit for a sibling's scenario is the wrong place.

card.ifOverturned: A: scenarios need a per-unit owner before units can land. B: the census only reports.

forks.title: S-transport: how agreed observations reach the compiler

card.problem: Only design.json and graph.json reach a scaffolder or lane today (VERIFIED-FACTS 0.6). Observations will live in the session feed (ESAS-287): ops.jsonl in the main checkout, or the hosted design_maps projection. The committed design record is docs/prs/<id>/map.json (structureVersion 2), carried byte-for-byte to lanes. This depends on ESAS-287's storage decision.
useCases: Compile at the end of /design in the main checkout
Recompile in a lane or in the local gate
A struck observation disappears from the dashboard

options.label: Committed map.json carries agreed observations (design-map projects them at /design Step 4); the compiler reads --map

walks.text: Given an agreed observation in the feed; when /design writes map.json; then the observation is in the committed file, and the compiler reads the same bytes in any checkout.
walks.given: an agreed observation in the feed
walks.then: the observation is in the committed file, and the compiler reads the same bytes in any checkout

options.label: The compiler reads the live store (get_map / readMap)

walks.text: Given a lane worktree; when the compiler runs there; then ops.jsonl is absent (main checkout only), so it cannot compile.
walks.given: a lane worktree
walks.then: ops.jsonl is absent (main checkout only), so it cannot compile

options.rejectedBecause: Input is not reproducible outside the main checkout.

options.label: A separate committed observations.json per design folder

walks.text: Given an agreed observation; when /design writes both files; then a second committed document must be kept consistent with map.json.
walks.given: an agreed observation
walks.then: a second committed document must be kept consistent with map.json

options.rejectedBecause: Two committed records of one design.

recommendation.why: It is the only committed, lane-reachable design record that exists. It obliges ESAS-287 to give observations a structureVersion-2 home (schema bump plus PL copy).

card.ifOverturned: With B, compilation works only in the main checkout with the store present. With C, ESAS-287 owns a second committed document.
